# Scalar initial-image bitset: API and evidence audit

Current runtime: `c98d12582a138d5898e94908ee6690dda73998ca`. Thingsboard latest reached **run-2**; complete and accepted report **run-1**. This note audits a possible next design. It does not change runtime code.

## Measured identity pattern

The census completed on existing MAT indexes in300.47622033953667s with24g and2CPUs. It counted7,514,636 occupied scalar point cells, matching the overview's7,514,636 point-owned physical ConclusionGroup objects. There are5,923,972 identity-only cells (78.832454%). Static identity-only cells total5,325,214 (70.864563% of all cells,97.753342% of static cells).

There are6,122,471 literal identity header occurrences and exactly6,122,471 unique physical headers. Their shallow bytes total244,898,840. Thus these fact headers are not shared across cells. There are2,754,298 unique trie root objects for these headers. Zero literal identity TAINT headers have a non-null nonSubsumable mask in this snapshot. The census checks this field for each matching TAINT header; an absent protectedIdentityHeaders counter means observed zero, not an omitted scan.

TbKafkaProducerTemplate.addAnalyticHeaders has617static premises,28occupied static identity indices, and17,104static identity-only cells; its simple product is17,276. It has17,282occupied cells overall. This is a measured premise × point pattern. It does not prove which operation first produced every row.

## Unique private wrapper objects and a lower bound

`MethodEdgeStore.add` creates a fresh ConclusionGroup for one previously empty `(premise,statement)` array slot. It does not assign that object to another slot. ConclusionGroup eagerly creates its own BooleanArray(2), Flow HashMap(2), and Taint HashMap(2). These fields are private, and no code reassigns them to another group's containers. This establishes uniqueness by source. The equal physical/logical cell counts also confirm it at this snapshot.

The measured shallow sizes give this gross private wrapper cost for static identity-only cells:

```text
5,325,214 * (ConclusionGroup32 + Boolean[2]24 + FlowHashMap48 + TaintHashMap48)
=809,432,528bytes
```

This excludes TaintGroup/FlowGroup objects, layer arrays, ArrayLists, hash tables, entries, fact headers, trie nodes and marks. It is not a retained-byte attribution to identity content. It is not a net saving: the replacement needs its own maps, bitsets and fallback state. The entire premise-array shallow size is only129,494,896bytes, so changing array capacity alone cannot remove most of the3,431,625,208-byte point-store owner union.

## Safe compression boundary

The fast representation can recognize one complete `initialFacts(I)` image, with the offered layer kept separate. It must compare:

```kotlin
premise is InitialAp
same base value
same entire single field path
same tail and field exclusion
FLOW: empty mark exclusion and the sole FLOW leaf
TAINT: the same sole mark, in the same exact or any slot
```

An EXACT concrete initial uses an exact leaf and canonical `anyTail=ANY_TAINT`, as `initialFacts` specifies. Non-empty field exclusions remain valid; compare their values. Do not require Empty E in this optimization. An ND premise, extra path, extra mark, different base, changed header or unsupported annotation uses the scalar store.

Store NORMAL and DEMAND memberships independently. The current method store separates layers; this optimization must not replace a DEMAND bit merely because a NORMAL bit exists. Preserve protection upgrades separately. For a normalized single-path/single-mark image, the valid mask is empty or the full sole image. If a mask is neither empty nor equal to that image, use the scalar fallback. A new protection bit is a new T2 observation and must emit the full protected image once; a repeated bit emits nothing.

## Interaction with an existing scalar cell

The fast path cannot deduplicate independently of an existing scalar ConclusionGroup. It must preserve ordinary merge/subsumption against competing facts. A conservative design is one-way promotion:

```kotlin
if (cell already has a scalar group) {
    return scalarGroup.add(offered)
}
if (offered is a supported complete initial image) {
    return addIdentityBitsWithLayerAndProtection(...)
}
val group = new ConclusionGroup(...)
materialize all currently stored identity bits into group // no enqueue
clear the compressed bits for this point
install group as the permanent scalar owner for this point
return group.add(offered) // only this fresh delta may enqueue
```

Materialization must reconstruct the exact current headers and masks. Do not replay already admitted identity deltas. Keep the producer-S admission gate and the next-relevant delivery algorithm. Do not introduce a destination-input history or change the queue contract. Packed run-1/FULL point storage can stay as-is; this candidate applies to scalar storage.

`edgesAt` has no production caller in the current core/JVM implementation. Its test/debug view must still materialize compressed cells. The `edgesAt(node,pattern)` view must continue to return the whole matching current value. The normal `add` API must still return exactly the fresh result, or the full value on a protection upgrade, and null for a duplicate.

## Tests/proofs required by the future proposal

Compare the expanded compressed view to the scalar reference after every operation, including both layers, full protection upgrades, duplicates, nonempty E, exact/STAR/ANY/must images, multiple contextual methods and point indices. Test promotion when a wider ANY, another base, an extra branch, another mark, or an exclusion change arrives. Verify both insertion orders and annotation upgrades during promotion. Keep cycle, diamond CFG, call shortcut and terminal-handler tests under the producer-S contract. The optimization changes representation only; it must not drop non-subsumable flags or loosen demand restriction.

## Other measured owners

CFG cache union is54,054,040bytes in the overview; the detailed census has303,188cached queries and341,680destination indices. This is not a main memory owner.

JVM forms keep808,391cached instruction copies across73,668context forms and51,952physical methods, with424,197distinct physical method/direction/instruction keys. Thus384,194instruction-key copies are redundant across contexts. Their footprint sets and map object headers are small compared with point cells. Sharing this method-only metadata is a valid separate candidate.

Static output indexes have172,945objects. FULL and fullInGroup each post3,047,219ordinals. The GROUP map is null in every object. fullInGroup owns29,157,960bytes in posting arrays plus5,462,408bytes in map headers, before entries/tables. These are current index costs, not net incremental costs versus the former trie.

Ordinary queues have373,980pending scalar inputs and2,872exact duplicate object triples, a lower bound. Queue backing capacity is2,847,458for other and633,529for ZERO. These counts do not establish a large duplicate backlog as the primary heap owner.

The JSON files beside this note embed the complete counts and top owners. `summary.json` binds their SHA-256 hashes. The source/bundle hashes and failed initial decoder attempt are preserved. No matching old heap was read, so this audit does not assign the whole current point-store union to the c98 change.
